nodes.label: USB HD Webcam (Microsoft LifeCam-style)
nodes.description: Close-up photograph of a black cylindrical Microsoft-branded HD USB webcam clipped to the top bezel of a laptop/monitor. Visible: 'HD' marking above the lens, a fixed glass lens in a ribbed barrel, a blue activity/status LED below the lens, a hinged tilt joint, and a rubberised monitor clip embossed 'Microsoft'.
nodes.rationale: A UVC-class USB webcam is used as the image capture device because it is plug-and-play on Linux (no driver work), mounts flexibly on an enclosure wall via its clip/tilt hinge, and can be placed away from the board unlike a short CSI ribbon.

nodes.label: Vision Image Capture Input
nodes.description: The role the webcam plays in the system: it is the sensing front-end that produces the image frames consumed by the on-device computer-vision/classification pipeline, complementing the non-visual gas/environment sensors.
nodes.rationale: Visual inspection captures conditions (appearance, behaviour, physical state) that chemical and thermal sensors cannot express, so the design pairs an imaging modality with scalar sensors for a fuller state estimate.
